finalText:
This is almost always about **referential equality**, not actual prop value changes. Common causes, roughly in order of likelihood:

1. **New object/array/function literals on every render.** Even if the *values* are the same, `{}`, `[]`, and inline arrow functions create a new reference each render. `<Child config={{a: 1}} onClick={() => foo()} />` fails a `Object.is`/shallow-equal check every time.
   - Fix: wrap with `useMemo` (objects/arrays) or `useCallback` (functions), or hoist static values outside the component.

2. **No `React.memo` on the child.** By default, a function component re-renders whenever its parent re-renders, regardless of props. `React.memo(Child)` adds a shallow prop comparison to skip re-rendering when props are unchanged.
   - Fix: `export default React.memo(Child)`.

3. **`children` prop as JSX.** `<Parent><Child /></Parent>` creates a new `children` element on every parent render unless the JSX is hoisted or the parent itself doesn't re-render.

4. **Context changes.** If the child consumes a Context (`useContext`), it re-renders whenever that context value changes — even if the props you're passing directly are stable. A common trap: the context *value* object is recreated each render (`<MyContext.Provider value={{a, b}}>`), so every consumer re-renders on every provider render.

5. **Passing new object references from `useState`/`useReducer` unintentionally**, e.g. spreading into a new object each time instead of only updating on real changes.

Quick way to confirm which one it is: install the **React DevTools Profiler**, check "Highlight updates when components render," and look at the "Why did this render?" info — it'll tell you exactly which prop reference changed.

If you paste the parent/child component code, I can point to the exact cause.
